title: GATE Physics Topic Test: Electronics — Set 1
titleEn: GATE Physics Topic Test: Electronics — Set 1

questions.questionTextEn: In a step-graded abrupt p-n junction diode, how does the depletion layer width $W$ depend on the total reverse bias plus built-in voltage $V_0 + V_R$?
questions.explanationEn: Solving Poisson's equation for an abrupt step junction gives $W \propto \sqrt{V_0 + V_R}$ (hence junction capacitance $C_j \propto (V_0 + V_R)^{-1/2}$).

questions.questionTextEn: A Schmitt trigger circuit built with an op-amp employs:
optionsEn: Positive feedback to introduce hysteresis (two distinct upper and lower threshold voltages)
questions.explanationEn: Positive feedback creates two separate switching thresholds ($V_{UT}$ and $V_{LT}$), providing noise immunity through hysteresis.

questions.questionTextEn: In a BJT, the common-emitter current gain $\beta$ and common-base current gain $\alpha$ are related by:
questions.explanationEn: From $I_E = I_B + I_C$ with $I_C = \alpha I_E$, $I_B = (1 - \alpha)I_E$, so $\beta = I_C / I_B = \frac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha}$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to the Barkhausen criterion for sustained sinusoidal oscillations in a feedback amplifier with open-loop gain $A(j\omega)$ and feedback factor $\beta(j\omega)$, the loop gain $A\beta$ at the oscillation frequency $\omega_0$ must satisfy:
optionsEn: $|A\beta| = 1$ and total loop phase shift $= 0^\circ$ (or $360^\circ n$)
questions.explanationEn: Sustained constant-amplitude oscillations require unity loop-gain magnitude $|A\beta| = 1$ and positive feedback phase $\angle(A\beta) = 0^\circ$ (or multiples of $360^\circ$).

questions.questionTextEn: Which BJT amplifier configuration provides a $180^\circ$ phase shift between input and output voltages along with high voltage gain and high current gain?
questions.explanationEn: The Common-Emitter (CE) configuration inverts the signal ($180^\circ$ phase shift) and offers both high voltage gain and high current gain.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about Digital-to-Analog Converters (DACs) and Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs) are TRUE?
optionsEn: A Flash ADC is the fastest architecture, requiring $2^n - 1$ comparators for $n$-bit resolution
An $n$-bit ADC divides its full-scale input range into $2^n$ quantization levels
A Dual-Slope integrating ADC is faster than a Flash ADC
A Successive Approximation Register (SAR) $n$-bit ADC completes a conversion in $n$ clock cycles
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are exact. Dual-slope ADCs are very accurate and noise-rejecting but slow ($O(2^n)$ clock cycles), far slower than Flash ADCs (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: An amplifier has open-loop gain $A = 100$ and negative feedback factor $\beta = 0.09$. What is the closed-loop gain $A_f = \frac{A}{1 + A\beta}$?

A Zener diode regulator has $V_Z = 6\text{ V}$, series resistor $R_S = 100\,\Omega$, and supply voltage $V_S = 12\text{ V}$. With no load connected ($R_L = \infty$), what is the Zener current $I_Z$ (in mA)?

An op-amp has a unity-gain bandwidth (gain-bandwidth product) of $2\text{ MHz}$. If configured as a non-inverting amplifier with closed-loop gain $20$, what is its $-3\text{ dB}$ closed-loop bandwidth (in kHz)?
questions.explanationEn: $\text{BW} = \text{GBW} / A_v = 2000\text{ kHz} / 20 = 100\text{ kHz}$.

questions.questionTextEn: An ideal voltage amplifier has a power gain of $1000$. What is this power gain expressed in decibels (dB)?

In a fixed-bias silicon BJT circuit ($V_{BE} = 0.7\text{ V}$, $\beta = 100$) with $V_{CC} = 10.7\text{ V}$, $R_B = 500\,\text{k}\Omega$, and $R_C = 2\,\text{k}\Omega$, what is the collector-emitter voltage $V_{CE}$?
questions.explanationEn: $I_B = \frac{V_{CC} - V_{BE}}{R_B} = \frac{10.0}{500\text{ k}\Omega} = 20\,\mu\text{A}$. $I_C = \beta I_B = 2\text{ mA}$. Thus $V_{CE} = V_{CC} - I_C R_C = 10.7 - (2\text{ mA})(2\text{ k}\Omega) = 6.7\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A 3-variable Boolean function $F(A, B, C)$ is implemented with a 4-to-1 MUX having select lines $S_1 = A, S_0 = B$ and data inputs $I_0 = 0, I_1 = C, I_2 = C, I_3 = 1$. Which circuit does this MUX realize?
optionsEn: Carry-out of a Full Adder ($AB + BC + CA$)
Sum of a Full Adder ($A \oplus B \oplus C$)
questions.explanationEn: $F = A'B'(0) + A'B(C) + AB'(C) + AB(1) = AB + BC + CA$, which is the majority / full-adder carry-out function.

questions.questionTextEn: The Boolean function $F(A, B, C) = \Sigma m(1, 3, 5, 7)$ simplifies to:
questions.explanationEn: Minterms 1, 3, 5, 7 are precisely all odd binary combinations (all rows with $C = 1$), so $F = C$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about op-amp circuits are TRUE?
optionsEn: An ideal op-amp integrator's DC gain is infinite, so practical integrators place a large resistor in parallel with the feedback capacitor to prevent saturation from input offset voltage
An instrumentation amplifier typically uses 3 op-amps to provide high input impedance on both inputs and high CMRR
An inverting op-amp amplifier has infinite input impedance seen by the source
A voltage follower has closed-loop gain $+1$, very high input impedance, and very low output impedance
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are exact. Because of the virtual ground at the inverting node, an inverting amplifier's input impedance is simply $R_1$, not infinite (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: A full-wave bridge rectifier with ideal silicon diodes ($V_D = 0.7\text{ V}$ each) is fed by a transformer secondary with peak voltage $V_m = 15.4\text{ V}$. What is the peak output voltage across the load resistor (in Volts)?
questions.explanationEn: In a bridge rectifier, TWO diodes conduct in series during each half-cycle, so $V_{\text{out,peak}} = V_m - 2V_D = 15.4 - 1.4 = 14.0\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A JFET has $I_{DSS} = 12\text{ mA}$ and $V_P = -4\text{ V}$. What is its maximum transconductance $g_{m0} = \frac{2 I_{DSS}}{|V_P|}$ at $V_{GS} = 0$ (in mS)?
questions.explanationEn: $g_{m0} = \frac{2(12\text{ mA})}{4\text{ V}} = 6\text{ mS}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A 10-bit ADC has a full-scale input voltage range of $0$ to $10.24\text{ V}$. What is its quantization step size (resolution, in mV)?
A series RLC resonant circuit has $L = 1\text{ mH}$, $C = 10\text{ nF}$, and $R = 10\,\Omega$. What is its quality factor $Q = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$?

A sinusoidal signal $V_{\text{in}}(t) = 2\sin(1000t)\text{ V}$ is fed into an ideal op-amp inverting integrator with $R = 10\,\text{k}\Omega$ and $C = 0.1\,\mu\text{F}$. What is the peak amplitude of the sinusoidal output voltage (in Volts)?
questions.explanationEn: Integrator gain magnitude at angular frequency $\omega$ is $\frac{1}{\omega R C} = \frac{1}{1000(10^4)(10^{-7})} = \frac{1}{1} = 1$. Thus peak output = $1 \times 2 = 2\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In an op-amp inverting amplifier with $R_1 = 4\,\text{k}\Omega$ and $R_f = 20\,\text{k}\Omega$, the DC supply rails are $\pm 12\text{ V}$ (output saturates at $\pm 12\text{ V}$). If $V_{\text{in}} = -3\text{ V}$, what is the actual output voltage $V_{\text{out}}$ (in Volts)?
questions.explanationEn: Ideal linear output would be $-(20/4)(-3) = +15\text{ V}$, which exceeds the $+12\text{ V}$ saturation limit, so the output clips at $+12\text{ V}$.
